chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abi Jamilyah from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the mute woman whose husband accuses her (of adultery), how does he perform the li'an (oath of imprecation)? He said: 'They are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever.'

key_terms.لاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُ: She is not permissible for him
key_terms.يُلاَعِنُهَا: He performs li'an (oath of imprecation) with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an when the wife is mute?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific juristic detail regarding the *li'an* procedure when the accused wife is mute (*kharsa'*), ensuring the husband's oath suffices for permanent separation (*tazwir*). Unlike temporary divorce (*mut'ah*) or revocable divorce (*talaq raj'i*), this ruling establishes that the marital bond is severed irrevocably, preventing any future remarriage between the same couple even after the death of one party. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the finality of *li'an* as a distinct mechanism for resolving adultery accusations without requiring four witnesses.
